findings.source_passage: Indeed, he felt it to be impossible--more, perhaps, because he could not believe in his own success where so many others had failed. The thing was too easy, therefore it could not be. The hole would be empty.
findings.source_locator: paragraph after Tommy's 'It's impossible!' speech, before Julius's 'I guess you're rattled now all right'
findings.why_it_matters: This passage carries significant interpretive weight: it articulates the psychological logic of disbelief in one's own success, a thematic note that distinguishes Christie's handling of the dramatic climax from mere adventure-story suspense. Its absence flattens the interior drama.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the three-sentence interior reflection verbatim or near-verbatim between Tommy's outburst and Julius's smiling response: 'Indeed, he felt it to be impossible—more, perhaps, because he could not believe in his own success where so many others had failed. The thing was too easy, therefore it could not be. The hole would be empty.'

findings.source_passage: "Sure thing. What else could it be?" "You are still young, Mr. Hersheimmer. At my age you will probably have learnt one lesson. 'Never underestimate your adversary.'" The gravity of his tone impressed Tommy, but had little effect upon Julius.
findings.source_locator: exchange between Julius and Sir James before Julius produces the gun
findings.why_it_matters: The narrator's commentary—'The gravity of his tone impressed Tommy, but had little effect upon Julius'—differentiates the two characters' sensibilities and foreshadows the chapter's ironic outcome. The draft omits Julius's prior 'Sure thing. What else could it be?' and the narrator's observation, losing the tonal contrast.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore Julius's 'Sure thing. What else could it be?' riposte and the narrator's beat 'The gravity of his tone impressed Tommy, but had little effect upon Julius' immediately after Sir James's maxim.

findings.source_passage: "I guess I'm ashamed to admit it, but I came over here determined to find her and fix it all up, and take her back as Mrs. Julius P. Hersheimmer!" "Oh!" said Tommy, amazed. Julius uncrossed his legs brusquely and continued: "Just shows what an almighty fool a man can make of himself!"
findings.source_locator: Julius's confession on the train, second paragraph of dialogue
findings.why_it_matters: The phrase 'Just shows what an almighty fool a man can make of himself!' is the comic punch of Julius's self-deflation; its excision and the physical gesture ('uncrossed his legs brusquely') together establish voice and character register. The draft collapses this into a bare paraphrase ('One look at the girl in the flesh, and I was cured!') losing the rhetorical shape.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore Julius's 'Just shows what an almighty fool a man can make of himself!' as a separate sentence following the revelation, and keep 'Julius uncrossed his legs brusquely' as the bridging action.

findings.source_passage: Tommy flushed. "Well, I'm damned! If that's----" Julius hastened to interrupt. "Say now, don't be hasty. I don't mean what you mean."
findings.source_locator: argument about French attitudes toward marriage, after Julius's 'romance and marriage apart' line
findings.why_it_matters: Tommy's hot half-sentence and Julius's clarification—'I don't mean what you mean. I take it Americans have a higher opinion of morality than you have even'—are voice-establishing exchanges that give the sparring its comic and moral texture; cutting them compresses the argument to a single exchange and loses the interplay.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore Tommy's 'Well, I'm damned! If that's——' and Julius's full clarification ('Say now, don't be hasty. I don't mean what you mean. I take it Americans have a higher opinion of morality…') before arriving at Tommy's 'we're all too damned businesslike' speech.

findings.source_passage: He slapped his pocket. "Little Willie here travels round with me everywhere." He produced a murderous-looking automatic, and tapped it affectionately before returning it to its home.
findings.source_locator: Julius showing gun to Sir James in the street
findings.why_it_matters: The original's 'tapped it affectionately before returning it to its home' is a character-defining gesture that voices Julius's showmanship; the draft replaces it with 'flashed a murderous-looking automatic,' losing the affectionate pantomime.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'tapped it affectionately before returning it to its home' in place of 'flashed.'

summary: The draft omits the chapter's most interpretively weighty interior passage (Tommy's psychology of disbelief in his own success) at high severity, and flattens three medium-weight voice exchanges—the narrator's differential-reaction beat after Sir James's maxim, Julius's self-deflating climax on the train, and the 'I don't mean what you mean' clarification—triggering regeneration.
